body: Jain, Khizer & Thirumalai studied 8,273 quarterly earnings-call transcripts from 559 S&P BSE 500 firms (2004-2019), measuring tone as optimistic minus pessimistic words. Optimistic tone produced positive short-window abnormal returns but did NOT predict better future operating performance. Retail investors reacted most, which the authors read as investors being misled. The paper is posted as an NSE white paper. Implication for our edge: in India, management cheerfulness is priced but uninformative, so scoring tone alone gives no edge and may push you the wrong way. The edge is checking stated promises against later delivery (the promise tracker). A 'tone minus credibility' gap is a candidate signal: high optimism with a poor delivery record should be overpriced, and understated managements with high delivery should be underpriced. This is a hypothesis to test on our own data. The sample is large caps; small-cap managements may be even more promotional.
title: India: optimistic concall tone moves prices but does not predict operating performance
